spec: Build a blog platform backend. Authors create posts with markdown bodies stored in DynamoDB and images stored in S3. Readers can list and read posts and submit comments. Comments are not published immediately: they are placed on an SQS moderation queue, and an approval endpoint pops them from moderation into the published comments table.

complexity.rationale: Content, media, and queued moderation form a multi-stage publication workflow.

congruence_checklist: DynamoDB storage for posts and comments
SQS moderation queue for new comments
GET endpoints listing and reading posts

plan.summary: A FastAPI backend for a blog platform. Authors create, update and delete posts whose markdown bodies and metadata live in a DynamoDB table, and upload post images to an S3 bucket (served back via presigned URLs). Readers list and read published posts and submit comments; submitted comments are not written to the comments table directly but are enqueued as JSON messages on an SQS moderation queue. Moderators list pending comments by polling the queue, and an approval endpoint moves an approved comment into the published comments DynamoDB table (or discards it on rejection), deleting the message from the queue in both cases. The service runs as a standalone process and calls S3, DynamoDB and SQS directly with boto3.

endpoints.purpose: Create a new post with a markdown body and metadata; persists an item in the posts DynamoDB table.
List posts with pagination (scan/query the posts table), returning summaries without full markdown bodies.
Retrieve a single post including its markdown body and image references.
Update an existing post's title, body, tags or status in DynamoDB.
Delete a post from the posts table and remove its associated S3 image objects.
Upload an image (multipart file) to the S3 images bucket and attach its key to the post.
List the post's images with time-limited S3 presigned download URLs.
Submit a reader comment; serialises it and sends it to the SQS moderation queue instead of publishing it.
List approved/published comments for a post from the comments DynamoDB table.
Poll the SQS moderation queue and return pending comments together with their receipt handles.
Approve a pending comment: write it to the published comments table and delete the message from the moderation queue using its receipt handle.
Reject a pending comment: delete the message from the moderation queue without publishing it.
Liveness/readiness check reporting reachability of DynamoDB, S3 and SQS.

data_models.name: Post
fields: image_keys (list of string S3 object keys)

data_models.name: PendingComment
fields: receipt_handle (string, returned from SQS, not stored)

aws_resources.name: blog-posts
aws_resources.justification: Stores post items (markdown body, title, author, tags, status, image keys). Read/written by the /posts endpoints.

aws_resources.name: blog-comments
aws_resources.justification: Stores published comments keyed by post_id (partition) and comment_id (sort). Written by the approval endpoint and read by GET /posts/{post_id}/comments.

aws_resources.name: blog-post-images
aws_resources.justification: Stores uploaded post images; the image upload endpoint puts objects here and the image list endpoint generates presigned GET URLs.

aws_resources.name: blog-comment-moderation
aws_resources.justification: Holds submitted comments awaiting moderation; POST comments sends messages, the moderation listing endpoint receives them, and approve/reject delete them.

aws_resources.name: blog-comment-moderation-dlq
aws_resources.justification: Redrive target for the moderation queue so comments that repeatedly fail moderation processing are retained rather than lost.

aws_resources.name: blog-backend-service-role
aws_resources.justification: Role/policy granting the standalone backend service least-privilege access to the two DynamoDB tables, the images bucket and the moderation queues.

aws_resources.name: blog-backend-logs
aws_resources.justification: Log group for the backend's application and moderation-decision logs, plus a queue-depth alarm on the moderation backlog.

assumptions: No authentication mechanism was specified; endpoints are open and the author/moderator identity is supplied in the request body or an optional X-Author header. IAM guards only the AWS resources, not the HTTP API.

The backend runs as its own process (started by the harness) and uses boto3 against LocalStack endpoints; no Lambda or API Gateway is planned because moderation is driven synchronously by the approval endpoint rather than by cloud-side event processing.
Comment moderation is pull-based: GET /moderation/comments performs an SQS ReceiveMessage with a visibility timeout, and the client returns the receipt handle when approving or rejecting.
Post listing uses a paginated DynamoDB Scan with a limit and an opaque next-token cursor, since no access pattern for querying by author or date was specified.
Images are uploaded through the API as multipart form data (server-side PutObject) rather than via client presigned PUT URLs; downloads use presigned GET URLs valid for one hour.
The images bucket is private with public access blocked and versioning disabled; deleting a post deletes its image objects.
Post identifiers and comment identifiers are server-generated UUID4 strings; timestamps are UTC ISO-8601.
'Published' status for posts is a simple attribute flag; listing returns all posts unless a status filter query parameter is supplied.
Both DynamoDB tables use PAY_PER_REQUEST billing, which is the LocalStack-friendly default.
Rejected comments are discarded (message deleted) and only logged to CloudWatch; no rejected-comments table was requested.

events: 🧭 Parsed specification → blog_platform_backend (fastapi); AWS resources: DynamoDB:blog-posts, DynamoDB:blog-comments, S3:blog-post-images, SQS:blog-comment-moderation, SQS:blog-comment-moderation-dlq, IAM:blog-backend-service-role, CloudWatch:blog-backend-logs

🐍 Generated application code (initial): 7 files — Generated a FastAPI blog platform backend split into a routing layer (`app.py`), an AWS data-access layer (`storage.py`, boto3 behind the `BlogRepository` interface with `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`/us-east-1 support and env-driven resource names `blog-posts`, `blog-comments`, `blog-post-images`, `blog-comment-moderation`), and a stdlib multipart parser (`uploads.py`) so image uploads work without python-multipart. All 13 planned endpoints are implemented, including SQS-based comment moderation with approve/reject that delete the queue message and publish approved comments to DynamoDB. Tests (`tests/test_app.py`) drive every endpoint through `TestClient` with fake in-memory DynamoDB/S3/SQS clients injected via FastAPI dependency overrides, so they run fully offline; a root `conftest.py` handles importability, and requirements list only fastapi, uvicorn, boto3 and pydantic.

🏗️ Generated Terraform (initial): 4 files — Terraform for the blog platform backend, one-to-one with the plan's aws_resources list.

Files: `versions.tf` (terraform block pinning hashicorp/aws ~> 5.0 plus provider `default_tags` with project/managed-by), `variables.tf` (defaults exactly matching the plan names: blog-posts, blog-comments, blog-post-images, blog-comment-moderation, blog-comment-moderation-dlq, blog-backend-service-role, blog-backend-logs), `main.tf`, `outputs.tf`.

Resources:
- DynamoDB `blog-posts` (hash post_id) and `blog-comments` (hash post_id, range comment_id), PAY_PER_REQUEST, SSE enabled, point-in-time recovery enabled.
- S3 `blog-post-images` with SSE-S3 + bucket keys, versioning, full public access block, BucketOwnerEnforced ownership, server access logging to a dedicated `blog-post-images-logs` bucket (itself encrypted/versioned/blocked/self-logged with expiration lifecycle), lifecycle rules (abort incomplete multipart, non-current version expiration) and a bucket policy denying non-TLS access.
- SQS `blog-comment-moderation` with SSE-SQS, visibility timeout for pull-based moderation, redrive policy to `blog-comment-moderation-dlq` (also SSE-enabled) plus a redrive-allow policy on the DLQ.
- CloudWatch log group (365-day retention) with a moderation-decisions stream and an `ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible` alarm on the moderation queue.
- IAM role `blog-backend-service-role` with a least-privilege policy: scoped DynamoDB item/query/scan actions per table ARN, object-level S3 actions on the images bucket only, SQS send/receive/delete/visibility on the two queue ARNs, and logs write on the specific log group — no wildcard actions or resources.

No Lambda, API Gateway, RDS/ECS/EKS/ElastiCache or KMS resources are created (the backend runs as a standalone boto3 process). Where a Checkov check requires a KMS CMK, cross-region replication, or S3 event notifications that LocalStack Community or the plan does not support, targeted inline `#checkov:skip` comments with reasons are included instead of inventing unused resources.
